question: Why can no material wealth equal the value of the kaula teaching?
premises: One might possess immense accumulated wealth.
Even an ocean filled with jewels is imaginable wealth.
inference: Even one whose accumulation could fill the ocean with jewels cannot equal this teaching's worth.
uncertainties: The form ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is obscure and may be corrupt or highly fused.
plain_english: Even one whose accumulation could make the ocean filled with jewels.
